_about: Single source of cross-feature known risks for the « Éditeur de livre dont vous êtes le héros ». Aggregated from every features/*/specification.json plus the global engineering rules in SKILL.md/CLAUDE.md. Banded ids: 0xx = per-feature domain risks (stable, gaps expected); 1xx = global cross-cutting engineering rules. Ids are stable references — never renumber; append new ones at the next free id within the right band.

known_risks.risk: Seed must be atomic and EXACT: a book always contains exactly Sommaire + isolated Mort. Seed through one BookService factory, never ad hoc.
The Mort node is isolated by contract (0 edges) and obligatory; it is locked (not deletable/duplicable, type fixed, only text editable) and never auto-linked on create.
Book id is collision-free and stable; the id, not the title, is the persistence key. Ids via brain/utils/id. All references (objects, monsters, node targets) are by stable id, never by name.

Navigation and events fire only AFTER persistence resolves, in order (e.g. book:created -> book:opened). Listeners must always observe a persisted book. Any callback that closes over mutable state needs a stable ref.
No raw window.localStorage in feature files; persist only via PersistenceService and the key builders in persistenceKeys.ts. Feature-level facet of global KR-111.
No useEffect for derived state — compute inline or with useMemo. Legitimate useEffect: subscriptions, imperative DOM/third-party APIs, external-store syncing. Feature-level facet of global KR-113.

The canvas is a VIEW, not the model: never mutate node/edge data locally; all changes go through BookService so outline-view and game-preview stay consistent. Local-only edits desync the visualizations.
Orphaned edges (source/target node deleted) must be dropped or visibly flagged, never rendered as a line to nowhere or a crash. Reconcile on every render / node:deleted.

Pan/zoom and canvas<->outline view-mode are UI preferences (UIPreferencesService), explicitly NOT part of the synced book document; pushing them to CloudSyncService causes spurious conflicts (cloud-first boundary).

The canvas AUTO-LAYS-OUT the book as a top-down TREE (resolvePositions, a pure VIEW over the choice-edge structure, KR-020): a DFS of the choice hierarchy from the sommaire root assigns y by DEPTH (each level a row beneath the previous) and x by a left-to-right leaf cursor with each PARENT CENTRED over its children's span — so the sommaire is at the TOP, every node's direct children sit on ONE evenly-spaced horizontal row beneath it, recursively, and links read downward. Convergence/cycle targets reached via nesting are placed once (visited set, KR-080/061). LINKLESS / unreachable nodes (the isolated mort, any page not reached from the sommaire by a choice edge) WRAP INTO A GRID below the tree (FREE_COLS columns) — so a book of loose pages reads as a familiar grid while a connected book reads as the tree above it. Do NOT place free nodes in a single horizontal row (reads as 'all nodes horizontal') NOR a single vertical column (reads as 'one branch descending') — both regressed this and were rejected; a wrapping grid avoids both. Deterministic, stable across reloads, never a 0,0 pileup. Stored node.position is currently IGNORED by the view; manual drag + per-book position persistence is a later iteration, at which point a stored position overrides the computed slot. autoSlot remains the BookService document default but is not consulted for the canvas layout.

Node selection is the single source of truth in the brain SelectionService (promoted from tree-canvas local state). Canvas and node-editor both read via useSelectedNode and write via selection.select; the service is the sole emitter of node:selected and clears on book:opened. No feature keeps a competing copy (avoids two-panel desync).

Per-device editor view state (pan/zoom, canvas↔outline view-mode, dragged node positions, the outline collapsed-node set) lives in the brain UIPreferencesService, persisted through the RAW local store — NOT the CloudSyncService decorator — so it can NEVER enter the cloud queue (KR-022/093); createBrain wires it over `local`, not `sync`. Its key is the `genliv:ui:book:<id>` namespace (uiPrefsKey), distinct from BOOK_KEY_PREFIX so listBooks never sees it. DRAGGED POSITIONS are a UI PREFERENCE, not synced book content: they persist in UIPreferencesService keyed by book+node and OVERRIDE the computed auto-layout slot in resolvePositions (a stored override replaces the slot, but only for nodes still in the book — a deleted node's stale override leaves no ghost, KR-021/023); node.position on the document stays the autoSlot default and is not consulted by the canvas. The service serves reads from an in-memory CACHE so getBookPrefs returns a STABLE reference between writes (useSyncExternalStore requires snapshot stability — a fresh object each call infinite-loops); each write makes a NEW prefs object (immutable update) and notifies subscribers; the no-prefs snapshot returns a single frozen EMPTY constant. Hooks (useBookViewMode/useBookNodePositions) are external-store subscriptions (KR-013), never useEffect mirrors. The live viewport stays fast local useState seeded lazily from the service and PERSISTED ON SETTLE (drag-release, each zoom step, a centre request) — never every pan frame. NodeCard drag uses window pointer listeners tracked in a ref + unmount cleanup (no dangling listener, BUG-001 pattern); a press that travels past a threshold is a drag (commit position, consume the click), one that doesn't is a select.

node-editor is a HOST shell: the action body (PNJ/décor/piège/monstre) and the choices list are mounted from other features via ActionRegistry / feature slots. Importing an action feature directly would break feature isolation.

Adding a new action type must require ZERO changes to node-editor: the SegmentedControl options + the mounted editor come from the ActionRegistry. Hard-coding a type couples node-editor to a specialty (Open/Closed).
Objects carry a player-facing DESCRIPTION, not just a name; the inventory editor must capture both via the shared brain ObjectEditor, never a bare string (domain rule).

Selection swap must not leak the previous node's uncommitted field state into the next node. Bind fields to the store (no local mirror) and/or key the panel subtree by node id so it resets on selection change.

Turning a node into a Fin (victoire/échec) changes its kind/badge everywhere; the end flags live on the node in BookService and the FIN badge is derived (effectiveKind/endLabel) so canvas/outline/panel reflect it from one source via node:updated.

Sommaire (root) and Mort (death leaf) are STRUCTURAL screens: no « libellé du choix », no « action requise pour poursuivre », no Fin victoire/échec toggles. Mort additionally has NO outgoing choices. Their only editable field is the text. Enforce both in the UI (hide those sections) AND in BookService.updateNode (text-only patch for sommaire/mort), so the invariant holds at the SSOT, not just the panel.

Edges are the book's structure: all create/delete goes through BookService (addChoiceBranch/addEdge/removeEdge) so tree-canvas + outline-view + game-preview agree; never mutate edges locally (re-asserts KR-020). Mort may not have outgoing edges — enforced at the SSOT, not just the UI (KR-055).

Relink allows cycles/convergence by DESIGN but must guard degenerate cases: no duplicate identical edges, sane self-link handling, and the target node is never created/deleted by relinking (only the edge). Guards landed in iteration 2 at the SSOT (BookService.addEdge rejects from===to and any pre-existing from/to/kind edge — identity is from+to+kind, so a same-target edge of a different kind is legitimate convergence) AND mirrored in the relink picker (self + already-relinked targets excluded); the SSOT is the law, the picker is convenience.

Hidden prerequisite references an acquirable object by STABLE id, not by name; a dangling reference (the object was deleted, or none is chosen yet) must be DETECTED and surfaced, never silently treated as true/false. IMPLEMENTED (choice-linking iter 3) against a DERIVED catalog, not an owned store: brain/utils/objects.ts `collectObjects(book)` is a pure VIEW (KR-020) that unions every acquirable object already authored on a node (décor « prendre » takeables incl. the deprecated single `object`, the PNJ gift, the monster loot), de-duped by id — objects stay owned where they are authored (no separate ObjectCatalogService to desync), and the catalog is recomputed inline (KR-013). The rule lives on the choice EDGE as `Edge.prereq?: { objectId }` (`'' ` = chosen-but-unconfigured), persisted via BookService.updateEdge (EdgePatch `prereq: ChoicePrereq | null`, where null CLEARS the rule and an omitted key leaves it untouched — mirrors the label-drop pattern). The SSOT stores intent only; the VIEW validates the id against `collectObjects` / `findObject` and shows ⊘ when it resolves, ⚠ when it dangles. A future owned catalog (if objects ever need reuse independent of a node) can replace `collectObjects` transparently since everything already references by id.

Countdown fallback + relink targets are node references that can dangle if the target is deleted; run a referential-integrity check and surface broken targets rather than crashing the reader later (re-asserts KR-021).

Deleting a `choice` branch may orphan its child subtree; prompt/handle explicitly — do not silently leave unreachable nodes or cascade-delete without consent. Implemented: the row ✕ is confirmation-gated (DeleteBranchDialog over the brain Modal, confirmTone='error', dangerous-action rule); the dialog states the target NODE is never deleted (only the link) and warns when this is the node's SOLE incoming link (orphaning), computed live from the book. It still only removes the edge — the orphaned node survives (listed flat in the outline); a cascade 'also delete the node' affordance would need a BookService.deleteNode that does not exist yet.
A choice may hold BOTH a hidden prerequisite and a countdown; the countdown only ticks while the choice is visible (prerequisite met), so a hidden choice never expires invisibly.

Cross-feature panel composition uses the brain SlotRegistry: a host (node-editor) reserves a slot id (SLOT_NODE_EDITOR_CHOICES) and renders whatever is registered, falling back to a placeholder; a provider (choice-linking) registers a renderer at the composition root (App). Neither feature imports the other — same OCP seam as ActionRegistry, for arbitrary panel regions.

Structural screens are never authored choice targets: the Sommaire root has no incoming choices and the Mort leaf is reached ONLY automatically at the end of a combat, never via a choice/relink. Enforce at the SSOT (BookService.addEdge rejects a target whose kind is sommaire/mort) AND in the relink picker (exclude them from candidates), not just one. The automatic combat→Mort link uses a DEDICATED path, not the manual edge API — IMPLEMENTED (action-trap iter 2) as a VIEW-DERIVED edge: brain/deriveAutomaticEdges(book) emits a synthetic { kind: 'fatal' } edge from each fatal-trap node (actionType === 'piege' && trap.fatal) to the Mort leaf; the canvas renders authored + derived edges together (resolveEdges([...book.edges, ...derived])). Derived, NEVER stored — the config stays the SSOT so the link can't desync and never touches addEdge (KR-020/013). Gate on actionType (the action config key), not node.kind. The same helper generalises to the other deferred outcome targets (monster victoire/fuite/défaite, PNJ « mène à »). EXTENDED (action-trap iter 3): deriveAutomaticEdges now has a SECOND fatal source — a décor « prendre » takeable whose jet requis is fatal (SkillRoll.fatal) derives the same auto-fatal-<node>→Mort edge (trap-on-object). One edge per node (a node has one actionType, so the piège/décor branches never both fire); the helper stays brain-side and reads node.decor.objects inline (no action-decor import). The shared roll model is brain SkillRoll; the « Variante piège : échec → mort » toggle lives in action-decor ObjectEditModal — the two features share only SkillRoll + deriveAutomaticEdges, never import each other.

Per-kind knowledge lives in ONE data-driven registry (brain/kinds.ts: NODE_KINDS / EDGE_KINDS), not scattered if (kind === …) tests or partial maps. Each descriptor carries the kind's label, default title, badge mark, and domain invariants (structural / canHaveOutgoing / canBeTarget). Consumers (NodeBadge, nodeView, effectiveKind, NodeEditorPanel, BookService, EdgeLayer, OutgoingChoices) READ the descriptor. The registry is the SINGLE source even for the NodeKind/EdgeKind union types: each is derived with `keyof typeof` via the `defineKinds` factory, which infers the key union while pinning every entry to the descriptor shape — so there is no separate union to keep in sync, a missing descriptor field fails to compile, and there is no silent Partial<Record> gap. Kinds stay plain string literals (JSON-serialised domain) — descriptors, not classes, are the 'replace conditional with polymorphism' answer here. Same Open/Closed seam as ActionRegistry (KR-051). DOMAIN INVARIANTS are read through NAMED PREDICATES (kinds.ts: isStructural/canHaveOutgoing/canBeTarget/edgeNests), not by indexing the registry at call sites — callers ask the question without importing NODE_KINDS/EDGE_KINDS or knowing its shape (Law of Demeter); the registry stays the single source. PRESENTATIONAL reads (label/mark/defaultTitle/rowLabel/tone/canvasLabel) may still read the descriptor directly in view code.

Deleting a book is a dangerous, irreversible action: always gate behind a confirmation dialog (name the book, error-toned confirm, labelled Annuler) and route the delete through BookService.deleteBook (persist-remove then book:deleted, KR-004) — never a raw removal.

The library list is a VIEW over BookService via useBooks (recomputed only on book:created/book:deleted, cached snapshot for useSyncExternalStore), never a private copy (re-asserts KR-020/013). Search/sort over it must be DERIVED INLINE (filter + sort a COPY — never mutate the cached snapshot array, or useSyncExternalStore's stable reference breaks). Deleting the currently-open book could leave the editor on a dangling route — guarded (iteration 2) at the COMPOSITION ROOT (App subscribes to book:deleted, reads the router route fresh in the handler, navigates home if the deleted id is open in the editor), not in the feature, so no feature owns cross-route navigation and there is no stale-closure route dependency.

book-creation and book-library compose at the app root: LibraryScreen receives the create affordance as a prop (<CreateBookEntry/>); neither feature imports the other (feature isolation). Same composition-root seam as the ActionRegistry/SlotRegistry, for a sibling screen rather than a panel region.

The outline DFS MUST guard cycles/convergence: a node already shown — or reached via a relink/flee edge — becomes a ↪ reference row and is never recursed into, so a cyclic book (allowed by design, KR-061) cannot infinite-loop. Nodes unreachable from the sommaire root (the isolated mort, free-floating nodes) are listed flat so none are hidden. A dangling edge target is flagged (⚠ cible supprimée), never crashed (KR-021). buildOutline is pure + view-agnostic so the rule is tested once.

A cross-view IMPERATIVE action (« Centrer dans l'arbre »: outline asks the canvas to switch-to-tree + centre on a node) is wired at the COMPOSITION ROOT (EditorScreen), never feature-to-feature: the shell owns a {nodeId, seq} request, the source feature calls an onX callback prop, the target feature receives the request as a prop. Do NOT use a bare event bus for an action whose target may be UNMOUNTED at emit time (the canvas isn't rendered while the outline shows) — the event fires before the target mounts and is lost (the navigate-then-act timing trap). A shell-owned prop is read by the target on mount, so the action survives the view switch. A monotonic `seq` makes repeat requests distinct (same node twice still re-acts); a consumed-seq ref guards the effect so an unrelated re-render (e.g. positions changing on a book edit) never re-fires. The relation summary (buildNodeInspector) is pure + view-agnostic like buildOutline, tested once; dangling source/target titles resolve to null, never crash (KR-021).

An action-* feature self-registers its editor with the brain ActionRegistry at the composition root (registerActionDecor) and persists its config ON THE NODE document via BookService.updateNode — never feature-local state, never a node-editor import (KR-050/051/020). Décor config lives at node.decor (DecorConfig); NodePatch carries it so updateNode's text-only guard keeps it off structural screens (sommaire/mort, KR-055). The takeable object is captured via the shared brain ObjectEditor (name internal + player-facing description, KR-052) with a stable id minted once via createId (KR-003); embedding it on the node is the skeleton. REUSE-BY-ID across nodes (décor iter 3) landed NOT as an owned ObjectCatalogService but as a DERIVED REFERENCE (user decision, the same call as KR-062's derived catalog): a TakeableObject is EITHER « own » ({ object }) OR a « ref » ({ objectRef }) reusing an existing catalog object by stable id; `object` is now OPTIONAL on the type, exactly one of object/objectRef set. takeables.ts helpers takeableId / isRefTakeable / resolveTakeableObject(book, t) (own → inline object; ref → findObject(book, objectRef), null = dangling ⚠ KR-021) keep callers off the optional field. collectObjects SKIPS refs (a ref is not an authoring source — its object lives on the owner node), so no phantom catalog entry and no desync (the object stays single-sourced, KR-020). « Prendre dans la liste » (ReuseObjectPicker) lists collectObjects minus already-present ids and adds a ref; a ref row is READ-ONLY in the décor editor (edit the object on its origin node). The ObjectEditModal only ever edits an own takeable. A future owned catalog could still swap in transparently since everything references by id.

Combat/skill outcomes are réussite/échec ONLY — the only semantic outcomes and the only semantic colours (réussite = good/green, échec = bad/red). Their label + tone live in the brain ROLL_OUTCOMES registry (Record<RollOutcome,{label,tone}>, an instance of KR-117), placed in brain (not the feature) because trap + décor/PNJ skill-roll editors will reuse it (KR-109). Editors DERIVE every outcome row from ROLL_OUTCOMES — never hardcode « Réussite »/« Échec », never branch on the value, never invent other outcome colours. The monster library is wired via the monster:savedToLibrary event (per the event list) but stubbed: no consumer/persistence until the MonsterLibraryService iteration (like the deferred Object/PNJ catalogs).

A trap is a réussite/échec skill roll: its outcome reveal rows reuse the SHARED brain OutcomesEditor (KR-109) derived from ROLL_OUTCOMES (KR-117/091) — never a per-feature copy of the rows or the labels (the rows were extracted to brain at the SECOND consumer, monster→trap, like ObjectEditor). The « échec sanctionné » variant is a fatal boolean on node.trap capturing intent; the actual automatic échec→Mort edge is wired later via the dedicated combat/trap path, NOT the manual edge API (KR-067). Trap config lives on node.trap and rides updateNode's text-only structural guard (KR-055/090).

CloudSyncService is a Decorator over PersistenceService (Liskov) wired once in createBrain — features stay unchanged. It MUST be local-first: get/set/keys/remove hit the local store synchronously so the app works offline and the synchronous write resolves before any event/navigation (KR-004); the cloud push is best-effort in the background and never blocks/reorders the local write, and a failed push keeps the local write (status → error). With no transport the store is `offline` (local-only) and emits sync:status ONLY on a real change (no per-write noise) — so wrapping is transparent to non-sync code. Only the book document flows through persistence; UI state (view-mode, pan/zoom) is never synced (KR-022). The SyncStatus→label/tone mapping is one Record (KR-117); a real transport's credentials must be registered SENSITIVE in persistenceKeys.ts (KR-114).

The CloudTransport is selected by BUILD/PRODUCTION TARGET at the composition root (main.tsx): the local target wires a localStorage-backed LocalStorageTransport (a fake remote in a separate `cloudsync:` namespace), the Cloudflare target a worker-backed one; both implement one interface so app code is target-agnostic and tests stay offline by default (createBrain transport-optional). Pushes are DEBOUNCED + BATCHED — set() writes local synchronously then coalesces into a pending map flushed after a debounce window; status goes syncing (sync on write) → synced/error once per batch; the flush timer is tracked + cleared on reschedule. book:opened triggers LAST-WRITE-WINS reconciliation by updatedAt: a newer cloud copy is adopted by writing the UNDERLYING local store (NEVER the decorated set — avoids re-pushing what was just pulled, no echo loop) then emitting book:updated so open views re-read; a newer local copy is pushed up; an empty cloud is seeded. Reconciliation is the ONLY place the persistence decorator is book-aware (resolves bookKey, emits book:updated). Extends KR-093.

The pending pushes are an OFFLINE QUEUE persisted locally (CLOUDSYNC_QUEUE_KEY, in the genliv namespace via the UNDERLYING local store — never the decorated set, no echo; not a book key, so listBooks ignores it), LOADED at startup so an unconfirmed write survives a reload. A FAILED push KEEPS the queue (status → error) — never drop the batch (the pre-iter-2 behaviour lost it); on success dequeue ONLY the entries actually pushed (queue.get(key) === pushed value — a newer write to the same key during the in-flight push stays queued), guarded by a `flushing` flag against double-push. Flush-on-reconnect has three triggers: the next write, an explicit retry(), and STARTUP (a persisted backlog schedules a flush). pendingCount() surfaces « N changements en attente » via a useSyncPending external store (KR-013); the sync:status payload carries `pending`. Keep emits STATUS-change-only (no per-keystroke noise) — offline the status toggles syncing↔error per write so the count stays live; do NOT also emit on every pending delta (that re-broadcasts an online burst). This UNBLOCKS book-creation iter 3 (cloud-first offline create). PER-BOOK sync status (book-library iter 3) reads the GENERIC pendingKeys(): string[] (the queued storage keys) — the decorator stays book-agnostic (KR-094, it never resolves bookKey here); the book→key mapping lives in the brain useBookPending(bookId) hook (bookKey(id) ∈ pendingKeys), re-read on every sync:status emit (same cadence, no extra events). The card then shows « à jour » / « en attente » / « non synchronisé » (offline = no chip, local-only). List reconciliation (pulling cloud-only books) and offline DELETE propagation need new CloudTransport capabilities (list + delete) and stay deferred to a cloud-sync iteration. Extends KR-093/094.

REUSABLE entities across nodes (action-pnj iter 3: « réutiliser un PNJ du livre ») follow the same DERIVED-REFERENCE pattern as the object catalog (KR-062/090), with one twist: a PNJ has no id of its own, so the OWNER NODE's id IS the PNJ's stable id (KR-003) — no separate id field, no minting, no migration. A node's PnjConfig is EITHER own (authored fields) OR a ref ({ pnjRef: ownerNodeId, name:'', dialogue:'' }, the other fields unused). action-pnj/utils/pnjCatalog.ts: collectPnjs(book) = own PNJ nodes (actionType 'pnj', pnj set, no pnjRef) keyed by node id (refs skipped — not an authoring source, so no phantom entry); resolvePnj(book, node) resolves own → its config, ref → the owner's config LIVE (null when the owner was deleted, is no longer a PNJ, or is ITSELF a ref — refs do NOT chain, surfaced ⚠ KR-021). The PnjEditor shows a ref READ-ONLY (resolved identity + « réutilisé » badge + « défini sur <owner> », a « Ne plus réutiliser » detach back to an own empty PNJ); the PnjPicker (mirrors ReuseObjectPicker) lists collectPnjs minus self. The object stays single-sourced on its origin node (no desync, KR-020); collectObjects is unaffected because a ref pnj stores no gift (the owner's gift is counted once from the owner). updateNode replaces node.pnj wholesale, so reuse/detach write the full canonical shape.

The reusable MONSTER LIBRARY (action-monster iter 3) is a PERSISTED CROSS-BOOK store (brain MonsterLibraryService over the RAW local store under MONSTER_LIBRARY_KEY, not a book document, not cloud-synced), DISTINCT from the within-book derived references (KR-062 objects / KR-096 PNJ which resolve live): different books can not share a live reference, so a library monster is INSTANTIATED as an independent COPY — save() deep-clones + STRIPS node-specific targets (victoryTarget/fleeTarget), instantiate deep-clones onto the node with a FRESH loot id (KR-003, no cross-use collision) and keeps the node own targets. list() is cache-backed for useSyncExternalStore stability (useMonsterLibrary hook, KR-013); save also emits the long-wired monster:savedToLibrary event (consuming the previously-stubbed path). The MonsterLibraryPicker mirrors the action-decor/pnj reuse pickers (copy-not-share, the 3rd reuse picker — extract a shared brain primitive if a 4th appears, KR-110).

Any presentational component consumed by more than one feature belongs in brain/components/ and is re-exported from brain/components/index.ts. A component living in a feature but imported by another is a cross-feature violation — move it.
Any utility used by more than one feature belongs in brain/utils/, never in a feature's own utils/. Importing from a sibling feature's utils/ is a cross-feature violation.

No raw window.localStorage in feature files — use PersistenceService for the book document and useUIPreferences()/UIPreferencesService (via brain/) for non-synced UI state. Single auditable storage surface.
Component/hook size limits: a file over 400 lines is a split signal (extract subcomponents/hooks); a file over 800 lines is a merge blocker.
No useEffect-synced mirrors of props/derived state; never use // eslint-disable react-hooks/exhaustive-deps to mask a stale closure — fix the root cause (stable refs, recompute inline).

Any localStorage key holding a credential/token/secret (PAT, OAuth, API key) must be registered in brain/persistenceKeys.ts with a /* SENSITIVE */ marker and annotated in UIPreferenceKey — one auditable location for all credential storage. None yet.

A design value needed both as a CSS string and as a numeric JS value lives in TWO synced forms: a CSS token (e.g. --hit-target: 44px in styles/tokens) and a mirrored brain constant (e.g. HIT_TARGET_MIN = 44 in brain/ui.ts). Use the token in CSS/style strings and the constant only where a number is required (numeric size props). The two MUST stay in sync — never reintroduce the bare literal at call sites.

PersistenceService.get does an unchecked JSON.parse cast, so persisted data is UNTRUSTED at the runtime boundary even though it is typed: a corrupted store or a schema drift can carry a node/edge kind outside the registry, and a direct NODE_KINDS[kind].field then throws (undefined access). Validate kinds at the single read boundary (BookService.loadBook + listBooks) with isNodeKind/isEdgeKind; a book with an unknown kind is surfaced (console.warn) and treated as unreadable (getBook/openBook -> null, omitted from listBooks, mutations refused) — never silently coerced. A corrupt book must remain DELETABLE (deleteBook uses the raw read, not the validated one), so the user can clean it up.

A closed set (a fixed union type — node/edge kind, décor interaction, action type, skill outcome…) lives in ONE Record<Union, Descriptor> as the single source of per-variant data + behaviour; derive option lists / labels / flags / copy from it, and NEVER re-list the literals or branch on the union with if (x === 'a') … else … or x === 'a' ? … : … ladders. This eliminates the Fowler/Uncle-Bob smells Duplicated Code, Repeated Switch/Conditional, Shotgun Surgery, Primitive Obsession, and honours Open/Closed + SRP — adding a variant is one new entry with zero consumer edits. In TypeScript the data-driven Record IS 'replace conditional with polymorphism' for a JSON-serialised domain (not a class hierarchy): use Record<Union, …> for compile-time exhaustiveness — never Partial<Record<…>> (silent gaps) — and derive the union from the keys (keyof typeof + a defineX factory) when the registry must be the single source for the set itself. Instances: NODE_KINDS/EDGE_KINDS (KR-068), ROLL_OUTCOMES, CHARACTERISTICS, GIFT_EFFECTS, TAKEABLE_KINDS, DECOR_INTERACTIONS. The editor only needs each variant's DATA (labels/tones/flags); when PLAY MODE lands, per-variant BEHAVIOUR (how to apply a gift effect, compute/test a caractéristique, resolve a leurre) becomes a descriptor FIELD on the same Record ({ label, apply, test, … }) — never an if/switch at call sites. Adding behaviour is one edit to the registry, the same Open/Closed win.
